title: Initiatives-to-Launch Map and OKR Alignment Canvas
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: produce a lightweight, actionable alignment canvas that maps active OKRs and initiatives to concrete launch windows across the runtime, console, and API release trains. The canvas will be used by PM leads, Eng managers, and Design to: 1) surface hard timing conflicts, 2) define gating criteria and SLO/metrics required for go/no-go, 3) assign clear owners for rollout phases and rollback lanes, and 4) construct an automated feed into the launch calendar so downstream teams see capacity/priority impacts. Scope: focused on Q2 initiatives and any high-risk Q1 carry-overs that touch serving runtime, Console dashboards, or API contract changes. Deliverables: - One-page alignment canvas (editable Confluence + PDF) - Launch calendar automations spec (GitHub issue + lightweight API contract) - Gating checklist template per release train (runtime/console/api) - Risk register and escalation playbook - A 30-minute cross-functional review session and sign-off checklist
comments: 2026-02-20 Sofia Martinez: Kickoff - draft canvas hypothesis posted to Confluence. Invited ENG, Design, SRE leads. Called out three initial problem areas: overlapping canaries, shared infra quotas, and uncoordinated feature flags.

2026-02-26 Ethan Blake: Spoke with Runtime leads (Mei Chen, Arjun Rao). Runtime requests a stricter latency gating clause for any rollout that modifies KV caching behavior. Proposed automatic fallback policy if p50 increases >15% during canary.

2026-03-02 Priya Kapoor (Design): Provided initial calendar UX mock in Figma. Feedback: calendar needs a layered view (OKR -> Initiative -> Release Train) and a conflict heatmap overlay. Will iterate on Monday.

2026-03-03 Liam O'Sullivan (SRE): Noted capacity reservation constraints for Dedicated pools during regional spikes. Suggested 'reserve window' field per launch entry and a dependency flag for Dedicated tickets.

2026-03-05 Product Review: PM/Eng sync - decision to implement two enforcement levels for gates: advisory (alerts only) and hard (block merges until met). Trade-off: hard gates increase coordination overhead but reduce rollbacks.

2026-03-08 Ethan Blake: Drafted automation spec to emit conflict alerts to #launch-calendar Slack channel and create a blocking Linear ticket when two P0 initiatives overlap the same release train in the same week.

2026-03-09 Design feedback incorporated into Confluence canvas. Added quick filters: by OKR owner, by tag (privacy/compliance), and by release-train. Preparing presentation for 2026-03-12 launch sync.

2026-03-10 Sofia Martinez: Updated ticket - consolidated gating checklist and linked GH backlog mapping. Next: validate with Legal for any privacy/compliance labeled initiatives before sign-off. Assigned follow-ups to Eng and SRE owners.
next_steps: 1) Run 30-minute cross-functional review on 2026-03-12; 2) Finalize gating language with Runtime and SRE by 2026-03-16; 3) Ship initial calendar automation MVP that posts overlaps to Slack by 2026-03-24; 4) Add Legal/Compliance sign-off step for privacy-labeled initiatives.
acceptance_criteria: - Canvas approved by PM leads and Runtime/Console/SDK Eng leads; - Gating checklist templated and reviewed; - Automation MVP creates alerts for overlapping P0/P1 launches in test workspace; - Documentation linked from each release ticket to the canvas
